The atlas uses an invalid demonstration code. Each PC receives its own revocable access.

Using an older invite?

TS1 needs a separate Host address. TS1 and TS2 keep their original expiry; they need a Host-assigned server after pairing.

A few steps to play

  1. Connect to the Host with its current server code.
  2. Wait for approval if the Host requires it.
  3. Choose an assigned server, review its game requirements, then join in the game.

Join makes an outbound connection. This PC does not need an inbound port forward.

dialogs.title: Staging test with another owned PC
dialogs.description: Host fixture preparation and Friend connection/chat/transfer rehearsal with seven independent evidence stages.
dialogs.html:
Development / staging only

Use a disposable synthetic server, separate access and ports. No real game runs and production worlds are separate.

  1. Development Host: prepare Connection rehearsal.
  2. Test PC: pair its development Friend app normally to that fixture code.
  3. Host: grant Receive. Friend: verify group and explicitly allow local saves.
  4. Test PC: choose the disposable server and owner-reported network context, then run rehearsal.
  5. Review separate stages and copy a redacted report.

Physical network is not inferred from this selector. Outside TCP and human game checks never pass from synthetic chat or transfer.
